title: LotusWorks security & hosting intake - KMS / SSO / retention
summary: Initial security posture discovery to map LotusWorks requirements for hosted vs dedicated vs private Redwood deployment. Main concerns: BYOK/KMS key wrap, SSO/SAML flows, RBAC & audit logs, data retention/erasure, and SOC2 evidence. Agreed to follow up with architecture diagram, security docs link, and schedule an engineering deep-dive plus pilot/benchmarks.
action_items: Samira Patel (SE): Produce KMS architecture diagram showing hosted vs Private VPC + customer-wrapped keys (due 2026-03-14)
Jordan Kim (AE): Share SOC2/ISO pack + encryption whitepaper link to LotusWorks (due 2026-03-09)
Marcus Reed (Customer): Provide list of required audit log fields and retention duration (due 2026-03-12)
Alicia Gomez (Customer): Confirm compliance constraints around data residency (due 2026-03-11)
Evan Lu (SE): Pull example RBAC role matrix from similar retail customer (due 2026-03-16)
next_steps: Send SOC2/ISO certs and security whitepaper (Jordan)
Schedule architecture deep-dive to walk through Private deployment diagram (Samira/Evan with LotusWorks infra) — proposed 2026-03-15
Set up short pilot: 2-week Dedicated capacity trial with KMS wrapping tests (if NDA signed)
Customer to provide requirements spreadsheet for logs/retention and regulatory hold needs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Lu (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (LotusWorks), Marcus Reed (LotusWorks Sec), Alicia Gomez (LotusWorks SRE), Tom B. (LotusWorks Legal), Ruben (Data Privacy)

[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, I'm Jordan, AE, and Samira and Evan are our technical leads. how's everyone?
[00:18] Priya Menon: Hi, thanks. we're eager to understand how Redwood would fit into our inference stack, specifically security posture stuff. we run sensitive customer telemetry and some pii-ish metadata, so encryption and retention is the big one.
[00:33] Marcus Reed: yeah we have SOC2 in progress and we're trying to map vendor controls. if you support BYOK or HSM integration that would be a big plus.
[00:45] Samira Patel: totally. we support a few patterns — hosted with customer keys in KMS, dedicated with managed keys, and Private deployment where keys never leave customer control if you want to run our control plane in your VPC. i'll try to sketch the differences as we go.
[01:05] Alicia Gomez: can you clarify "customer keys in KMS" — does that mean Redwood ever sees the unwrapped key material?
[01:13] Evan Lu: good question. short answer: in hosted we can integrate with cloud KMS with customer-managed keys — key material doesn't leave the cloud provider. we do have an option for key-wrapping where the customer holds the root wrapping key in an HSM and we never have access to the unwrapped root. but the transcript note: sometimes we say "BYOK" or "customer-wrapped" and the flows vary by cloud.
[01:36] Marcus Reed: so what's the threat model — if a Redwood-hosted node is compromised could they decrypt token caches?
[01:44] Samira Patel: for hosted endpoints we use envelope encryption: model weights stored encrypted at rest, per-request payloads encrypted in transit and at rest; KV cache is encrypted and access-controlled. For highest assurance you want Private with customer-managed HSM or dedicated capacity with key wrapping.
[02:05] Priya Menon: we need to satisfy legal: no plaintext customer data stored beyond X days, and ability to prove deletion on request. how do you handle retention and deletion requests?
[02:18] Jordan Kim: Redwood supports retention configs per route; by default we have short-term ephemeral caches and we offer longer retention policies if you opt-in for analytics/quality monitoring. For request erasure we provide an API and can provide logs showing the deletion action — will share specifics in the SOC2 doc.
[02:37] Ruben: do you keep raw transcripts for summaries? we don't want raw PII left around.
[02:42] Evan Lu: it's configurable. hosted default tiling is ephemeral, but some customers enable longer retention for evals — when enabled we mask or hash depending on config. we'll show the retention controls in the deep-dive.
[02:58] [03:00] Tom B. (Legal): i want to understand custody of keys for each deployment variant and whether Redwood signs or can provide attestations. also we need timeline for SOC2 evidence.
[03:11] Jordan Kim: we'll share our SOC2 report and if you need vendor attestations we can provide the security pack. we can also discuss contractual clauses around key custody in the SOW.
[03:24] Marcus Reed: SSO is another major item for us — we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. does Redwood support SAML SSO and SCIM?
[03:33] Samira Patel: yes, SAML 2.0 for authentication and SCIM for user provisioning and group sync. RBAC in the console can be mapped to your groups, and we support custom roles. sometimes provisioning attribute mapping needs a quick mapping doc which we can send.
[03:50] Priya Menon: do you support SCIM for service accounts or just human users?
[03:55] Evan Lu: both — service principals can be managed via the API and we have token scoping: tokens can be bound to models, routes, and TTLs. we recommend short-lived tokens and scoped roles for automation.
[04:12] Marcus Reed: audit logs are critical. which events are logged and for how long? retention and immutability are big concerns.
[04:20] Samira Patel: we emit detailed audit logs: auth events, model invocation metadata (not full prompt unless enabled), key usage events for KMS calls, admin actions (role changes, config updates), and deployment events. retention is configurable — default 90 days, enterprise tiers go to 3 years with log export to your S3/GCS bucket for long-term retention and WORM-like behavior.
[04:47] Priya Menon: export sounds good. do you support pushing logs to our Splunk or sending to an S3 bucket with kms-encrypted objects?
[04:55] Evan Lu: yes we support push to SIEM via secure forwarding and export to customer buckets encrypted with their KMS key.
[05:03] [05:10] Jordan Kim: quick note — some of our larger fintech customers do a daily log ingest to their SIEM and keep a hashed prompt reference, that's fairly common.
[05:20] Marcus Reed: about RBAC — can we create roles that prevent developers from changing retention or enabling long-term storage?
[05:27] Samira Patel: yes, our RBAC supports per-action permissions; you can separate "admin:infra" from "admin:privacy" type roles. we can show the role matrix examples in the deep-dive.
[05:39] Priya Menon: SOC2 scope — are you SOC2 Type II? any ISO certs?
[05:44] Jordan Kim: we are SOC2 Type II and pursuing ISO27001; i'll attach the cert and the control mapping.
[05:52] Alicia Gomez: do you provide FIPS 140-2 HSM integrations if we need government-grade key wrapping?
[05:57] Evan Lu: we have partners we integrate with who have FIPS HSMs — in Private deployments you can bring your own HSM. for hosted we can integrate cloud KMS which often offers FIPS-mode.
[06:10] [06:30] Marcus Reed: encryption in transit — TLS, mTLS options?
[06:34] Samira Patel: TLS everywhere, and for Dedicated and Private we can do mTLS between services. we also support mutual TLS for customer-to-runtime connections.
[06:44] Priya Menon: any data residency guarantees? we have EU customers and need EU-hosted keys and compute.
[06:51] Jordan Kim: yes region pinning is supported — compute and keys can be pinned to specific regions; Private deployment gives full control over physical location.
[07:03] Ruben: how do you handle legal hold or e-discovery?
[07:08] Evan Lu: we can pause deletion for a route and export the data to a customer bucket for legal hold workflows; this is often a manual process with governance approvals.
[07:20] Marcus Reed: curious about metadata in logs: do you log full prompt text by default?
[07:25] Samira Patel: no, default is to log metadata (timestamps, user id, model id, token counts) but not full prompt text unless explicit retention/quality monitoring is enabled. if you enable it we recommend token redaction and hashed identifiers.
[07:40] [08:00] Priya Menon: okay this is helpful. can you walk through a concrete example: we want to run a POC on Dedicated capacity, have customer-wrapped keys in AWS KMS with an external key encrypting the KMS key (double-wrap), and enforce RBAC such that only platform ops can toggle retention. how would that look?
[08:20] Samira Patel: sketch: Dedicated GPU pool in our managed account or in a customer-dedicated account, KMS in your account with Customer Managed CMK, we perform envelope encryption and we support external wrap where the root wrap key is in your HSM. RBAC enforced via SCIM group mapping to the "retention.admin" role. logs pushed to your S3 bucket with server-side encryption using your CMK. we'll diagram this.
[08:50] Marcus Reed: what's the rollout time for Private vs Dedicated?
[08:55] Jordan Kim: Dedicated can be spun up in a few days once contract and onboarding are done. Private (VPC + control plane), depending on network approvals and we might do an on-prem appliance, takes 4-8 weeks typically.
[09:07] Alicia Gomez: pricing tradeoffs — Dedicated reserved capacity vs hosted per-token?
[09:12] Jordan Kim: tradeoff is cost predictability vs lowest initial cost. Dedicated is predictable commit with lower per-token price at scale; hosted is pay-as-you-go. Private adds engineering onboarding and license fee. we'll share a pricing template.
[09:30] [09:45] Tom B. (Legal): for contract we need specific SLA statements around key custody and incident notification windows — 24 hour notification for security incidents?
[09:55] Jordan Kim: typical is 24-hour initial notification and dedicated incident channel for enterprise customers; we can include that in the SOW.
[10:05] Marcus Reed: do you provide proof of deletion? we need an auditable trail.
[10:10] Evan Lu: yes we provide deletion logs and can export a signed artifact showing deletion timestamps. we can also run a mutual attestation if you want crypto proofs — it's more complex but doable.
[10:26] [10:40] Priya Menon: any references of customers in regulated industries?
[10:44] Jordan Kim: we've worked with a couple of fintechs and healthcare analytics teams — not naming here on call but will include anonymized case studies in the pack.
[10:55] Marcus Reed: one more technical — how do you handle model updates and rollbacks without exposing data?
[11:01] Samira Patel: model variants are stored encrypted and model rollout is route-based. KV cache is isolated per-tenant and scrubbed on route deletion. we'll show the rollout controls in the console.
[11:18] [11:30] Priya Menon: ok, looks like we have a plan. what do you need from us right now to proceed?
[11:36] Jordan Kim: the main things: a list of required log fields/retention, a contact for legal to receive SOC2 pack (Tom), and decision on pilot scope. we'll send a short questionnaire.
[11:50] Tom B. (Legal): i'll take SOC2 pack and the contract redlines once you send draft.
[11:56] Ruben: i'll work with Marcus and Alicia on retention specifics.
[12:03] Jordan Kim: great. we'll follow up with the docs and propose a deep-dive time. thanks everyone.

Notes / small errors: occasional mention of "KV cash" in transcription should be read as KV cache. Redwood product names sometimes said as "red wood" or "redwood dedicated" spelled differently.

References shared: Redwood security pack link (placeholder): https://redwood.example.com/security-pack.pdf, RBAC matrix: https://redwood.example.com/rbac-sample.xlsx, KMS pattern diagram (will be attached).

End of transcript.
